BiblicalUsage: Ezra the scribe appears in this form in the Aramaic of King Artaxerxes' letter, where the king addresses him as Ezra the priest, a scribe of the law of the God of heaven, in Ezra 7:12. The same letter gives him authority over the treasurers beyond the river in Ezra 7:21, so that whatever he requires for the house of God is done speedily. The name stands in a foreign king's decree because the king recognised the God Ezra served.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Ezra's standing came from the law he carried, not from any office he held. A pagan king honoured him because he was a scribe of the law of the God of heaven, and I hold that devotion to God's word still commands respect in places we would not expect.
